articles.title: BOJ Ueda’s Absence Fuels Market Nerves Over Press Conference
articles.summary: Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda’s hospitalization is generating uncertainty among investors over the central bank’s messaging at its policy meeting next week, even as they remain convinced officials will raise interest rates.

articles.title: Indonesian Bonds Resume Decline as Market Confidence Stays Weak
articles.summary: Indonesia’s  bond selloff resumed on Thursday after a surprise interest-rate hike earlier this week provided only temporary relief, with investors once again focusing on the broader economic concerns that have fueled a market rout.

articles.title: US Asks to Drop Iran Sanctions Case Against Turkey’s Halkbank
articles.summary: The Justice Department asked a judge to let it drop a long-running US criminal case against Turkish state-owned lender Turkiye Halk Bankasi AS over alleged Iran sanctions violations.

articles.title: Danantara Starts Bond Sale in Test After Indonesian Selloff
articles.summary: Indonesia’s sovereign wealth fund Danantara kicked off its debut global dollar bond sale, testing investor appetite at a time when confidence in Southeast Asia’s largest economy has soured.

articles.title: Thai Long Bonds Draw Funds With Steepest Curve in Emerging Asia
articles.summary: Thailand’s yield curve has shifted to the steepest in emerging Asia, with some investors saying that makes its longer-dated bonds look attractive given a divergence in interest-rate expectations there versus regional peers.

articles.title: SpaceX IPO Is Said to Be Over Four Times Oversubscribed
articles.summary: SpaceX's initial public offering has attracted demand for more than four times the available shares, according to people familiar with the matter. Bloomberg's Michael Hytha breaks down the latest developments. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Investor Tied to Troubled Bank Loans Charged With Fraud by US
articles.summary: A California real estate investor whose firm was accused by Western Alliance Bancorp of an almost $100 million fraud was criminally charged by the US, the latest fallout from a portfolio of commercial properties that sparked credit concerns at several banks last year.

articles.title: India Turns to Military to Beef Up Security After Exam Scandals
articles.summary: India is taking unprecedented measures to restore confidence in its national student examination system after a series of scandals fueled angry protests from young people and put pressure on Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government.

articles.title: Activist Elliott Hits Back at Gold Miner Northern Star Over Sale
articles.summary: Activist investor Elliott Investment Management LP has hit back at Australia’s biggest gold stock Northern Star Resources Ltd. by urging the beleaguered miner’s board to take urgent action and reconsider a sale as its valuation flounders.

articles.title: New Zealand Primary Exports Seen Slower After Stellar 2026 Gain
articles.summary: New Zealand’s target of doubling primary exports by 2034 remains in place even as the stellar growth of recent years is tipped to slow in the face of geopolitical and weather challenges.

articles.title: US Launches Second Round of Strikes on Iran
articles.summary: The US military launched strikes against "multiple" targets in Iran for the second day in a row after President Donald Trump accused the country of dragging out talks on an interim peace deal. Bloomberg's Laura Davison explains the context. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Global Junk Debt Flashes Warning on Growing Risk of Stagflation
articles.summary: Fears of a stagflation shock from the Middle East conflict are increasingly souring investor sentiment toward the weakest global corporate borrowers, many of which binged on cheap debt during the era of ultra-low interest rates.

articles.title: Westpac Mortgage Applications Fall as Tax Changes Sap Demand
articles.summary: Westpac Banking Corp. mortgage applications are heading for the worst quarter in a year as tax changes for property investors weaken demand for real estate.

articles.title: How AI Is Changing Asia’s Workplaces
articles.summary: Financial heavyweights in Hong Kong including Baidu CFO Henry He and BlackRock's APAC Head Susan Chan share their insights on how AI is changing their workplaces. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Highlights from Bloomberg Invest Hong Kong
articles.summary: Top voices in finance joined Bloomberg to discuss topics ranging from the impact of China's regulatory crackdown to the risk of a global tech selloff. Bloomberg's David Ingles and Yvonne Man break down the highlights. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Alcoa Shares Drop as Firm Warns Alumina Unit Is ‘Underwater’
articles.summary: Alcoa Corp. shares plunged after a company executive warned that its alumina business is facing losses from energy disruptions and the near-closure of the Strait of Hormuz.
